q: A company has 50 teams and 3 levels (viewer, editor, admin). Someone suggests one role for each team and level, like `editor-team-a`. What is the problem?
options: A role cannot have a dash in its name
You get 150 roles that nobody can keep straight. This is role explosion
Roles cannot be checked on the server
A role can only be used once per user
why: A role gives one answer for a whole kind of user. When you need "this team only", use a list on the item or a rule on a fact like `user.teamId === doc.teamId`.

q: You share one document with one friend. Which model fits best?
options: A new role for that friend
A rule on facts about the time of day
A list on the document (an ACL): one new line saying `friend: viewer`
Give the friend the admin role
why: A role is for a kind of user. A list on the item answers for one item, and sharing is one new row.

q: doc-1 has the list `{ ana: "owner", budi: "viewer" }`. Write needs level 2, and viewer is level 1. May Budi write? May Ana read doc-2, which does not list her?
options: Budi: yes. Ana: yes, because she owns doc-1
Budi: no. Ana: no, because she is not on the list of doc-2
Budi: no. Ana: yes, because owners may read everything
Budi: yes. Ana: no
why: Budi's level 1 is below 2, so no. Owning doc-1 gives Ana nothing on doc-2. "Not on the list" means no.

q: Ana has an editor grant on `folder-A`. Nobody shared `file-9` (inside folder-B, inside folder-A) with her. May she write to it?
options: No, because file-9 has no grant for her
No, because she would need a grant on folder-B too
Yes, because the best grant on the file or on any parent above it counts
Only if she is also an admin
why: The server walks from the file up through its parents and keeps the best level. Editor on folder-A is level 2, and write needs 2.

q: Siti is an admin. A partner app has a token for her with `scopes: ["read"]`. The app sends a delete. What happens, and why?
options: It is allowed, because Siti is an admin
It is denied, because both the role and the scope must say yes, and the token has no `delete`
It is allowed, because scopes only apply to viewers
It is denied, because admins may not use tokens
why: A scope is a limit on one token. The answer is the smaller of the role and the scope. A scope never adds rights.

q: A list page must show only the 12 documents Ana may open, out of 100,000. How do you build it?
options: Load a page of 20, then drop the ones she may not see in code
Load all 100,000 into memory, then filter
Put the permission in the query, for example a join on the grants table with an index on `user_id`
Hide the others with CSS in the app
why: If you filter after loading a page, pages come out short or empty. When the permission is in the query, every page is full and the count is right. Hiding things in the app is not security.
